key_insight: Program-as-Weights turns a natural-language function specification into a small neural artifact that can be executed locally, making LLMs act as tool builders rather than per-query solvers.
engineering_relevance: This enables cheaper, more reproducible, and offline-friendly alternatives to calling large hosted models for fuzzy tasks like log filtering, JSON repair, and intent ranking.
method: Train a 4B compiler on FuzzyBench to emit parameter-efficient adapters.
Run the compiled adapters on a frozen 0.6B Qwen3 interpreter.
Use the produced artifact repeatedly for fast local inference.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a 10M-example FuzzyBench dataset and that the 0.6B Qwen3 interpreter with PAW matches direct prompting of Qwen3-32B while using about 1/50th the inference memory and reaching 30 tokens/s on a MacBook M3.
watch_item: Performance likely depends on the quality and coverage of the compiled fuzzy-function specification, so robustness outside the FuzzyBench/task distribution may be a concern.
paper_title: Program-as-Weights: A Programming Paradigm for Fuzzy Functions
